problems: The blind guess (a standing figure in a tunic, with trousers and shoes) does not match the intended subject. The drawing reads as an oar: a split blade at top, a long shaft, and a T-grip at bottom.
The drawing is upright, with the blade at top and the grip at bottom, which is correct for an oar.

The blue silhouette is a real outline of the oar (blade, tines, shaft, grip). It is not a copy of the gold lines.

output.advice: Redraw at a larger scale so the oar fills more of the frame. Keep the split blade at the top with stars 4906 and 3786 on the two tine tips. Keep star 4147 on the shaft at the binding, and make the wrap ring larger so it reads. Widen the T-grip so the crossbar is clearly wider than the shaft, with stars 3909 and 3455 on its two ends. Keep splash stars 6061 (up-left) and 2762 (up-right) clear of the shaft. Reduce the gold lines so they do not cross the shaft or obscure the blue outline. Move the labels apart: put the two tine labels on opposite sides of their tips, and stagger the two grip labels above and below the crossbar.
